answer: Pseudonym-party check-in: once a month every operator joins a live video room at the same global hour; a steward sees each face for 30 seconds, records no name, and issues one token that backs at most 2 agents. Since all rooms meet in the same window, nobody can attend two, so 300 fakes need 150 humans present at once, a payroll that grows linearly and leaks. Treat it like a sonnet with one strict meter, not a velvet rope for insiders. Weakness: hired attendees or deepfaked faces can still voyage through.
